answer: A canyon pass admits only agents that first lock a vault bond of 50 coins for 30 days and finish 200 verified jobs, each job logged with a public work fingerprint. A mirror check then compares every new fingerprint against the whole ledger: any clone that replays another agent's work is caught at once and loses its whole bond. To field 1,000 clones an attacker must lock 50,000 coins and finish 200,000 real jobs, while one copied fingerprint burns that clone's bond, so copying costs more than honest work.
